title: IoC Dispose Stack Inverse Accumulator Synchronization & Lifecycle Epoch Caching
author: Brain Harness Autobiographical Reflection Engine (harness-reflector & harness-compass)
context: Dynamic service registration in micro-kernels appends inverse teardown closures to a LIFO stack. Revoking services without purging matching closures causes memory leaks and invalid invocations on container disposal. Repeated DAG sorts during plugin cascading transitions cause high compute overhead.
distilled_learning: # IoC Dispose Stack Inverse Accumulator Synchronization & Lifecycle Epoch Caching

claims.assertion: Untracked inverse effect closures accumulate in _dispose_stack across service overrides and revocations, triggering dead effect invocations upon container disposal.
Kahn's topological sort dependency graphs are invariant within lifecycle epochs and can be memoized to accelerate multi-plugin cascading operations.
